content:
julia (PM): uploaded initial PRD for the kernel-selector + KV cache rollout.
Link: https://redwood.internal/rd/prd/kernel-selector-v1

samir (runtime): skimmed. big +1 on having hard SLOs. a few clarifying q's below.

liz (eng-ml): note from model side — quantized variants produce slightly different softmax tail behaviour; we should include a QA subset of prompts.

mike (infra): capacity note: dedicating a low-memory GPU pool for quant-variant will reduce burst headroom by ~12% unless we rebind autoscaling. FYI.

samir (runtime): suggestion: split launch into two phases: (A) non-quant kernel selection + routing policies, (B) quant variant gated by perf/regression checks.

julia (PM): agree. draft launch gates in PRD: must pass end-to-end latency SLO (p50 < 70ms p95 < 220ms), mem-usage within target, no >1% quality regression on eval suite, and rollback time <10m.

liz (eng-ml): for quality regression: propose evaluations on these buckets: short instructions, long multi-turn, code-assist, and semantic-search prompts (embedding parity). we'll provide 500 prompt set each.

samir (runtime): edge cases I want called out in acceptance criteria:
- cold-start KV cache: prefix hit-rate should not drop p95 latency below SLO for first 200 requests
- KV eviction during long-context sessions: evictions must not corrupt cache state or return stale tokens
- kernel fallback: if chosen kernel fails mid-request, runtime should transparently retry on compatible kernel without changing output ordering

mike (infra): add infra acceptance: deployment must include canary traffic control (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on error-rate >0.5% or latency breach >2x baseline.

julia (PM): good. add guardrail: customer-facing config for "prefer-latency" vs "prefer-cost" routing. default is prefer-latency. must be configurable per-tenant.

samir (runtime): implementation note: kernel-selector will use a ruleset + learned estimator. initial ruleset: (model-size, seq-len, tenant-preference) -> kernel-profile. estimator will be trained from pilot telemetry.

liz (eng-ml): tracker item: we need model-drift checks for estimator inputs. if estimator makes >3% suboptimal picks by cost/latency in a day, auto-disable estimator and fallback to ruleset.

ada-bot: deploy-checklist created: PRD linked, QA prompts uploaded, perf harness targets: p50/p95, canary schedule. See /deploys/1761238910.

samir (runtime): tests: add unit for kernel negotiation when multiple kernels have same estimated latency — deterministic tie-break by kernel id.

mike (infra): ops playbook item: in case of KV corruption observed, automated rollback + cache-flush + notify oncall; manual verification steps included.

julia (PM): customer ask: AtlasPay requested immediate ability to pin to "prioritize-cost" across their Reserved pool. action: samir + mike to scope config + impact on SLAs.

samir (runtime): I'll scope. quick calc: enabling cost-prefer reduces median CPU/GPU utilization by 18% but increases p95 latency by ~8% in our internal sim. need sign-off from product.

julia (PM): put that in PRD under "customer-driven exceptions" and add required notification to customer when toggling (30d trial and monitoring).

liz (eng-ml): edge-case: streaming + kernel-switch mid-stream — must preserve token continuity. add a test harness: simulate switch at token 10k.

samir (runtime): noted. also adding: healthchecks for per-kernel memory regressions; eviction metrics emitted as histogram.

mike (infra): timeline ask: can we do phase A canary within 3 weeks? infra needs 1 week to prep capacity and 2 weeks for staged rollout.

julia (PM): target: phase A canary start in 3 weeks, phase B (quant) tentative 6 weeks pending QA/regression. I'll update PRD timeline.

samir (runtime): owners: samir — runtime implementation; mike — infra canary ops; liz — evals & QA; julia — PM/launch.

julia (PM): final asks before I mark PRD ready for RFC: writeboarding on the fallback semantics, clear canary rollback thresholds, and a short customer comms draft.

samir (runtime): will write fallback doc and a tiny state machine snippet. posting later today.

mike (infra): i'll open infra ticket for capacity prep and link it in PRD.

ada-bot: reminder set for PRD review in 48h.

julia (PM): thanks team — if no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll promote this to RFC and create an RFC thread. :thumbsup:
